profile.reading: Lumen Technologies traces back to 1930 when F. E. Hogan Sr. sold the Oak Ridge Telephone Company, a 75 subscriber operation, and grew over the 20th century through the Century Telephone Enterprises name adopted in 1971 and a public listing in 1978. In the 21st century the company completed a series of large acquisitions: Qwest in a 12 billion dollar stock for stock merger completed April 1, 2011, Savvis, a cloud infrastructure and hosted IT provider, for 2 billion dollars in 2011, and Level 3 Communications in a 25 billion dollar deal that closed November 1, 2017. The company was known as CenturyLink through this period and renamed itself Lumen Technologies in September 2020. Critically for this registry entry, Wikipedia confirms that on May 2, 2017 CenturyLink sold its entire data center and colocation business to funds advised by BC Partners, together with Medina Capital Advisors and Longview Asset Management, for approximately 1.86 billion dollars, retaining only a 10 percent equity stake in the resulting company, Cyxtera Technologies. This means facilities carrying the Lumen or CenturyLink data center legacy, including this registry row, are very likely now Cyxtera facilities rather than current Lumen Technologies operations, though this specific building individual post 2017 ownership was not confirmed this session. Lumen Technologies is headquartered in Monroe, Louisiana. No building specific address or individual MW figures were located in available sourcing this session.
